quote: Lite $5,750 Billed annually ... 2 BFF Front-Ends ... Standard $12,500 ... 10 BFF Front-Ends ... Advanced $24,900 ... 30 BFF Front-Ends ... Free for development, testing and personal projects. Only pay for production.

claim: Community Edition eligibility is revenue-based: <$1M USD annual gross revenue and <$3M USD capital, or non-profit with <$1M budget; excludes redistribution and customer-facing deployments.
quote: For-profit organizations with less than $1M USD projected annual gross revenue and access to less than $3M USD in capital facilities, or non-profit organizations and registered charities with a published annual budget under $1M USD.

claim: A standalone Duende BFF for a React SPA against Keycloak is ~50 lines of Program.cs (AddBff().AddRemoteApis(), __Host- cookie, AddOpenIdConnect to Keycloak, MapRemoteBffApiEndpoint).
quote: The BFF implementation is minimal - approximately 50 lines of configuration code in Program.cs ... MapRemoteBffApiEndpoint("/api", "https://localhost:5375/api").RequireAccessToken()

claim: Duende.AccessTokenManagement and the other Duende FOSS libraries are Apache-2.0 licensed and free.
quote: Duende's open source projects are released under the Apache 2.0 license.

claim: Microsoft ships an official BFF-with-YARP + Aspire sample for .NET 10, using MapForwarder transforms to attach the access token and a custom CookieOidcRefresher for non-interactive refresh.
quote: This version of the article covers implementing OIDC with the Backend for Frontend (BFF) pattern with YARP and Aspire.

claim: OidcProxy.Net is an LGPL-3.0 open-source identity-aware reverse proxy built on YARP implementing the BFF/token-handler pattern; supports Keycloak, IdentityServer, Auth0, Entra ID and OpenIddict.
quote: An extendible framework for .NET to implement the BFF Security Pattern (a.k.a. Token Handler Pattern) in Single Page Applications

claim: oauth2-proxy is an MIT-licensed reverse proxy providing OIDC authentication for many providers; latest v7.15.3 (June 2026).
quote: A reverse proxy that provides authentication with Google, Azure, OpenID Connect and many more identity providers.

claim: Hand-rolled token renewal is discouraged: race conditions, multi-instance token storage conflicts, and real incidents of tokens leaking to the wrong users.
quote: Instead of building token renewal from scratch, we'll use the production-tested Duende.AccessTokenManagement library. ... Race conditions when multiple requests need renewal simultaneously.

claim: .NET 10 breaking change: cookie auth returns 401/403 for known API endpoints (IApiEndpointMetadata) instead of redirecting to login.
quote: Starting in .NET 10, unauthenticated and unauthorized requests made to known API endpoints result in 401 and 403 responses rather than redirecting to a login or access-denied URI.

claim: Built-in OAuth 2 refresh-token support in ASP.NET Core is still an open issue (opened 2019), now milestoned .NET 11 Planning.
quote: OAuth 2 refresh token support ... Milestone: .NET 11 Planning

claim: Duende BFF is licensed as its own product (Starter/Enterprise editions), requires a licence for production, trial mode limits to five sessions per host (not technically enforced), validation is fully local, and small orgs are pointed at the community edition.
quote: The Duende BFF Security Framework requires a license for production use, with two editions available (Starter and Enterprise) ... In Trial Mode, BFF will be limited to a maximum of five (5) sessions per host ... All license validation is self-contained and does not leave the host. There are no outbound network calls related to license validation.

claim: Duende BFF server-side sessions (AddServerSideSessions, EF store) keep the cookie small and constant and allow revocation on back-channel logout.
quote: the cookie size will be very small and constant - regardless how much data (e.g. token or claims) is stored in the authentication session; the session can be also revoked outside the context of a browser interaction, for example when receiving a back-channel logout notification from the upstream OpenID Connect provider

claim: Duende BFF's CSRF protection requires only an X-CSRF: 1 header, which forces a CORS preflight for cross-origin calls and thereby isolates callers to the same origin.
quote: anti-forgery in BFF is implemented differently from ASP.NET Core: it only requires the presence of a X-CSRF: 1 header ... having this header triggers a CORS preflight request in the browser for cross-origin calls.

claim: Duende.BFF latest is 4.2.0 (2026-06-10), targets .NET 10.0, 4.7M total downloads, depends on Duende.AccessTokenManagement.OpenIdConnect.
quote: Duende.BFF 4.2.0 ... Target Frameworks: .NET 10.0 ... Duende.AccessTokenManagement.OpenIdConnect (>= 4.1.1)

claim: The DuendeSoftware/products repo hosts IdentityServer, BFF and the DPoP JWT-bearer extensions under Duende's proprietary licence.
quote: Duende BFF (Backend for Frontend) - Implements the BFF security pattern, keeping tokens server-side

claim: BFF v3 to v4 is a breaking upgrade: TokenType renamed to RequiredTokenType, RequireAccessToken() to WithAccessToken(), IUserService to IUserEndpoint, and a breaking DB schema change (UserSessions.ApplicationName to PartitionKey).
quote: This is a breaking database schema change. If you have multiple BFF V3 applications that share the same database table, you either need to update all BFF applications to V4 at the same time or use a new database for the upgraded BFF V4 application.

claim: Duende.BFF 4.1.2 (2026-03-13) targeted net8.0/net9.0/net10.0; 4.2.0 (2026-06-10) targets net10.0 only.
YARP is an MIT-licensed reverse-proxy toolkit from Microsoft, ~9.6k stars, latest 2.3.0; its README does not cover authentication.
quote: YARP ... is a project to create a reverse proxy server ... a reverse proxy toolkit for building fast proxy servers in .NET using the infrastructure from ASP.NET and .NET.

claim: Duende.AccessTokenManagement.OpenIdConnect gives automatic access-token lifetime management using the refresh token for calls on behalf of the logged-in user, and is Apache-2.0 open source.
quote: Automatic access token lifetime management using a refresh token for API calls on behalf of the currently logged-in user ... released as open source under the Apache 2.0 license.

claim: ASP.NET Core has no built-in OIDC back-channel logout: you implement the webhook, validate the logout token, persist to a distributed cache and check it on every request via a cookie event handler.
quote: a server implementation and provide a web hook for the identity provider (Keycloak) logout event ... The logout event is handled and persisted to a distributed cache.

claim: Yarp.ReverseProxy latest stable is 2.3.0 (27 Feb 2025) with 68.7M total downloads; no newer preview exists.
quote: Latest Version: 2.3.0 (released 2/27/2025) ... Total Downloads: 68.7 million

claim: oauth2-proxy can pass the access token as X-Forwarded-Access-Token (pass-access-token), the ID token as a Bearer Authorization header (pass-authorization-header), set-authorization-header only in nginx auth_request mode, supports cookie-refresh and a Redis session store.
quote: pass-access-token: pass OAuth access_token to upstream via X-Forwarded-Access-Token header ... set-authorization-header: set Authorization Bearer response header (useful in Nginx auth_request mode) ... cookie-refresh: refresh the cookie after this duration

claim: Duende BFF exposes /bff/user, /bff/login and /bff/logout, enforces an X-CSRF header on API routes, and keeps tokens on the server.
quote: /bff/user, /bff/login, /bff/logout ... Enforces anti-forgery (X-CSRF header) on API routes ... tokens never cross the trust boundary into the browser.

claim: Duende BFF's remote-API forwarder uses YARP internally (Duende.BFF.Yarp package) and maps remote APIs with MapRemoteBffApiEndpoint(...).WithAccessToken(RequiredTokenType.User), with automatic anti-forgery and token management.
quote: It uses Microsoft YARP internally, but is much simpler to configure than YARP ... These routes receive automatic anti-forgery protection and integrate with automatic token management.

claim: Duende BFF v4 shipped 2 December 2025 with multi-frontend hosting, OpenTelemetry and simplified automatic configuration.
quote: A single BFF instance can securely serve multiple React, Angular, Blazor, or Vue applications.

claim: Duende staff confirm the production licence key may be reused in dev/test/UAT; validation is local with no phoning home and no aggregation risk.
quote: We do not consider the key a secret, configuring the same key is absolutely fine ... the checks are all done locally (no phoning home)

claim: YARP performs no authentication unless the app configures ASP.NET Core auth; with OIDC the result is an auth cookie that flows to the destination as a normal header, and swapping to a bearer token requires custom request transforms.
quote: No authentication or authorization is performed on requests unless enabled in the route or application configuration. ... The authentication process can be configured in the proxy application and will result in an authentication cookie. That cookie will flow to the destination server as a normal request header. ... These swaps can be performed using custom request transforms.

claim: YARP request transforms are added programmatically via AddTransforms/AddRequestTransform, which is the hook for injecting an Authorization header.
quote: builderContext.AddRequestTransform(async transformContext => { transformContext.ProxyRequest.Headers.Add("CustomHeader", "CustomValue"); });

claim: Microsoft's .NET 10 BFF sample wires cookie+OIDC, uses MapForwarder with AddRequestTransform and GetTokenAsync("access_token") to attach the bearer token, calls AddHttpForwarderWithServiceDiscovery, and documents PAR as the default (PushedAuthorizationBehavior.UseIfAvailable).
quote: var accessToken = await transformContext.HttpContext.GetTokenAsync("access_token"); transformContext.ProxyRequest.Headers.Authorization = new("Bearer", accessToken);

claim: Duende.AccessTokenManagement.OpenIdConnect 4.2.0 (2026-03-18) is Apache-2.0 and targets net8.0/net9.0/net10.0.
A YARP-based BFF needs hand-written /bff/login, /bff/logout and /bff/user endpoints on top of AddCookie + AddOpenIdConnect; the walkthrough does not cover antiforgery or refresh.
quote: MapGet("login", ...) ... MapGet("logout", ...) ... MapGet("user", ...)

claim: Injecting the token into proxied YARP calls uses a RequestTransform plus Duende's GetUserAccessTokenAsync (because raw token retrieval doesn't handle expiry/refresh), and the Cookie header is stripped with RequestHeaderRemoveTransform.
quote: doesn't automatically handle token expiration and most importantly the refresh cycle when the token is expired

claim: A YARP BFF gateway in Aspire uses Yarp.ReverseProxy + Microsoft.Extensions.ServiceDiscovery.Yarp with AddServiceDiscoveryDestinationResolver() to avoid hard-coded destinations.
quote: builder.Services.AddReverseProxy().LoadFromConfig(builder.Configuration.GetSection("ReverseProxy")).AddServiceDiscoveryDestinationResolver()

claim: IHttpForwarder/MapForwarder provide direct forwarding without YARP's routing, load balancing or config discovery — the minimal proxy primitive.
quote: Some applications only need the ability to take a specific request and forward it to a specific destination. These applications do not need ... routing, load balancing, etc. ... app.MapForwarder("/{**catch-all}", "https://localhost:10000/", requestConfig, transformer, httpClient);

claim: damienbod's BFF sample uses plain cookie + AddOpenIdConnect (no Duende BFF), serves the SPA from wwwroot in production and uses YARP only in development to front the Vite dev server, with AutoValidateAntiforgeryToken on controllers.
quote: In production, the built Vue.js app is served from wwwroot ... AutoValidateAntiforgeryTokenAttribute()

claim: Microsoft's CookieOidcRefresher is 102 lines of hand-written refresh logic with no locking/single-flight, and its header comment links to dotnet/aspnetcore#8175.
quote: // https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/8175  internal sealed class CookieOidcRefresher(IOptionsMonitor<OpenIdConnectOptions> oidcOptionsMonitor)

claim: SaveTokens plus large claim sets overflow the ~4KB cookie / ~8KB header limits, causing HTTP 431 and silent auth failures; the preferred fix is server-side sessions / a custom ITicketStore, with chunking as a tactical stopgap.
quote: 4 KB limit per cookie ... 8 KB limit ... HTTP 431 Request Header Fields Too Large ... Fix #1 - Server-Side Sessions (Preferred) ... ChunkingCookieManager splits a single logical cookie ... at 3500 bytes

claim: Migrating a hand-rolled BFF to Duende collapses the custom BffController into app.MapBffManagementEndpoints(), the proxying into one line, and removes the custom CSRF middleware.
quote: Entire custom BffController class becomes one line: app.MapBffManagementEndpoints(); ... Custom CSRF middleware (app.CheckForCsrfHeader();) becomes unnecessary

claim: ardalis/BFF is a stale fork of the archived Duende BFF repository, not a maintained alternative.
quote: This is a fork of the original Duende BFF repository (forked from DuendeArchive/BFF)

claim: ASP.NET Core 10 shipped the cookie 401/403 change for API endpoints, authentication/authorization metrics, and WebAuthn passkeys; it announces no BFF, refresh-token or DPoP feature.
quote: By default, unauthenticated and unauthorized requests to known API endpoints protected by cookie authentication now return 401 and 403 responses instead of redirecting ... ASP.NET Core Identity now supports passkey authentication based on WebAuthn and FIDO2 standards.

claim: Independent round-up of .NET 10 auth changes confirms passkeys, the cookie 401/403 breaking change and new metrics, and lists no BFF or token-refresh feature.
quote: When an unauthenticated or unauthorized request is made to a known API endpoint, the handler will no longer issue a redirect

claim: DPoP support in ASP.NET Core is still open and milestoned .NET 11 Planning; the issue notes the only current options are Duende libraries or writing your own.
quote: The current option in .NET is to either use Duende libraries, or write your own DPoP-implementation on top of the existing authentication stack in aspnetcore.

claim: Pomerium is an Apache-2.0 identity-and-context-aware reverse proxy (zero-trust gateway), latest v0.32.9 (June 2026).
quote: an identity and context-aware reverse proxy

claim: traefik-forward-auth is an MIT-licensed minimal forward-authentication service for Traefik providing Google/OIDC login; latest tag v2.3.0.
quote: A minimal forward authentication service that provides Google/OpenID oauth based login and authentication for the traefik reverse proxy

claim: Traefik's ForwardAuth middleware only delegates authentication to an external service; Traefik OSS does not perform OIDC login itself (its OIDC middleware is a Hub/Enterprise feature).
quote: delegates authentication to an external service. If the service answers with a 2XX code, access is granted, and the original request is performed.

claim: nginx's auth_request module authorizes based on a subrequest result and does not implement OIDC itself.
quote: implements client authorization based on the result of a subrequest. If the subrequest returns a 2xx response code, the access is allowed. If it returns 401 or 403, the access is denied

claim: gogatekeeper is the maintained Apache-2.0 community successor to louketo-proxy, latest v4.10.0 (June 2026), supporting Keycloak OIDC discovery.
